purpose: Archived independent small-rover measurements; not used to fit BWR

source.title: Effects of wheel width on running performance of four-wheeled small lunar rover
source.authors: Kimitaka Watanabe, Moegi Maru, Masataka Kawaguchi and Kazuto Tanaka

rover.gravity_environment: Earth laboratory; physical rover mass 1.5 kg, not a lunar-gravity test

measurement.response: slip = 1 - ground_speed / wheel_rim_speed for forward driving
measurement.reported_statistic: mean with standard deviation plotted in the paper
measurement.extraction: Manual reading of magenta b60 mean-marker centers from native image 2 of PDF pages 6 and 7; no individual trials or standard deviations reconstructed
measurement.selection: b60 is the only tested width inside the Sutoh table's 50-150 mm width domain. The 10-degree marker is visibly resolved in both plots. Higher angles are outside the common contributing-curve support at this geometry.

comparison_limits: Geometry lies inside the table, but load, speed, soil and grouser transfer are provisional, not matched experimental conditions.
The source rover supports about 0.375 kg per wheel, versus 3 kg per wheel in the Sutoh geometry sweep.
The source uses 10 mm grousers and 12 grousers per wheel; the default smooth rigid cylinder does not explicitly model them.
Two soils at one supported geometry/angle cannot support a Pearson correlation coefficient or a universal correction factor.
Other widths below 50 mm, higher unsupported angles and stuck conditions are not assigned invented model predictions.
